meaning:
ἀνα-γινώσκω
(Attic ἀναγιγν-), [in LXX chiefly for קָרָא ;]
1. to know certainly, know again, recognize.
2. Of written characters, to read: Mat.24:15, Mrk.13:14, Act.15:31 23:34, Eph.3:4; with accusative of thing(s), Mat.22:31, Mrk.12:10 Luk.6:3, Jhn.19:20, Act.8:30, 32, 2Co.1:13, Rev.1:3; with accusative of person(s), Ἠσαίαν τ. προφήτην, Act.8:28, 30; before ἐν, Mat.12:5 21:42, Mrk.12:26 (so. ἐν τ. νόμῳ), Luk.10:26; before ὅτι, Mat.19:4 21:16; τί ἐποίησε, Mat.12:3, Mrk.2:25; pass. 2Co.3:2; of reading aloud (MM, VGT, see word), Luk.4:16, Act.13:27 15:21, 2Co.3:15, Col.4:16, 1Th.5:27 (M, Th., in l).†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: But he said to them, “Haven’t you read what David did, when he was hungry, and those who were with him;
He said to them, “Did you never read what David did, when he had need, and was hungry—he, and those who were with him?
He came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up. He entered, as was his custom, into the synagogue on the Sabbath day, and stood up to read.
Therefore many of the Jews read this title, for the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city; and it was written in Hebrew, in Latin, and in Greek.
He was returning and sitting in his chariot, and was reading the prophet Isaiah.
For we write no other things to you than what you read or even acknowledge, and I hope you will acknowledge to the end,
by which, when you read, you can perceive my understanding in the mystery of Christ,
When this letter has been read among you, cause it to be read also in the assembly of the Laodiceans, and that you also read the letter from Laodicea.
